EE here yes every bit of that is possible. Raspberry Pi would be fast enough to do all that and writing a simple python program to read multiple senors isn't hard, however SD cards are pretty fragile unreliable things and while you could probably power it from your bikes electrical system its going to be a power hog which probably makes it a poor choice. A pi 3 compute has 4gb of much more reliable eMMC storage but it will still have the same battery life issues and you'll need an adapter / breakout board or custom PCB to even power it up much less interface with any sensors. A properly configured Orange Pi variant thats got some eMMC might be the ticket, it will have roughly the same dimensions as a Raspberry Pi, the same pins, and run the same OS but it will be an even bigger power hog, and you've got a less well established ecosystem so getting some help if you get stuck might mean you've got to do a bit of guesswork based on what people with a Raspberry Pi say. Plus they come factory overclocked which makes them a little unreliable (stability and lifespan) unless you take the time to properly configure it to a more reasonable CPU clock frequency and behavior but they are more or less as cheap as a Raspberry Pi 3, its also not a bad idea to fit these with a heatsink or heatsink and fan. You'll get a feel for what you need as you start.

Your bike might have a diagnostics port of some kind and most of those sensors you've described are already there as part of the bikes normal operation, you might better off getting something to interface with and read that data at a regular internals instead of trying to wireup all your own sensors unless there isn't any kind of easy to access diagnostics ports. 6 But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that diligently seek him. - Heb 11:6 (KJV)

This verse lets us know for sure that we must have faith to be able to please God. Our faith in Jesus, and what He did for us, is what pleases God, and we must stay strong in this faith, and obey Jesus, to assure us of our eternal salvation (Hebrews 5:9). It takes faith to believe that there is a God, as we can not see Him with our eyes. This faith comes by reading, or hearing, the Word of God (Romans 10:17), as it is the faith of God that comes through His Word.

Notice that we must believe that God “is”, not that He was or is gonna be. We must know that God is real and alive to us now, for our faith to be working. We also must know (be assured of) that God will reward us when we diligently seek Him. This is why the bible tells us we must believe, when we pray, that we receive our answer for our prayers to work (Mark 11:24). That is what faith is, believing in something you haven’t seen, or that hasn’t happened yet. Faith is the substance of things not seen (Hebrews 11:1), and you must have faith that you will receive what you hope and pray for. God is a God of faith, and He gives us His faith when we are born again, as it is a fruit of the spirit (Galatians 5:22-23), and we receive it when we get born again. You must have God’s kind of faith to believe in Him and in the entire spiritual world out there that you can’t see. Praise God for giving us His faith to use.
